Theme

Latin word

probō

probō, probāre, probāvī, probātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive

approve, think well of; win approval for, make (something) acceptable to someone; prove, show (a thing to someone)

In this lexicon

  • approve

    the recommended word · classical · Ov. Ars 2.198–200; Ov. Met. 7.20 (Lewis & Short)

  • impress

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 4.14.1: quōs (librōs), ut spērō, tibi valdē probābō (Lewis & Short)

  • prove

    the recommended word · classical · Caes. BG 1.3.5: perfacile factū esse illīs probat; Cic. Tusc. 5.1: difficile est probātū; Traupman 366

Examples

  • quicquid probat illa, probātō; quod dīcet, dīcās; quod negat illa, negēs

    whatever she approves, approve; what she says, say; what she denies, denyOv. Ars 2.198–200

    In the entry for approve

  • istam tuam sententiam laudō vehementissimēque comprobō

    I praise that view of yours and approve it most heartilyCic. Imp. Pomp. 69 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for approve

  • Perfacile factū esse illīs probat cōnāta perficere

    He proves to them that it would be very easy to carry out their plansCaes. BG 1.3.5

    In the entry for prove

  • quod etsī difficile est probātū propter tam varia et tam multa tormenta fortūnae

    and though this is hard to prove, because of fortune’s many and various tormentsCic. Tusc. 5.1

    But what will you set against it, if I deny ever having sent you that letter? With what witness will you prove me wrong?Cic. Phil. 2.8
